title: Walking May Improve Your Attention Span - Nautilus
gist: A Scientific Reports study using 14 years of FitBit data on 3,000+ adults in the NIH All of Us program links more daily walking to better cognitive measures including sustained attention.

insights.claim: Baylor College of Medicine researchers analyzed 14 years of health data from over 3,000 adults aged 18 to 93 in the NIH All of Us Research Program.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Large wearable-linked cohorts are a growing evidence base.
insights.locator: Researchers from the Baylor College of Medicine

insights.claim: The study used FitBit step counts rather than self-reported activity, which is less accurate.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Objective wearable data improves reliability over self-report.
insights.locator: The team relied on daily step counts

insights.claim: Participants completed tests of sustained attention, cognitive control, delay discounting and emotion recognition; walking is linked to better attention span.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Supports a low-cost health intervention; correlational design.
